latin: De re definitiue concepta, primus conceptus qui habetur est conceptus uniuersalissimus.
latin_note: The 1487 reprint here substitutes the reading proper to 1>10 ('est conceptus rei conceptus proprius et convertibilis'), part of the same editorial confusion noted at 1>10 (Farmer's note at farmer1998:18731).
translation: Take a thing as grasped by its defining formula: the very first concept one forms of it is the maximally general concept.
translation_note: Sense checked; no further crux beyond the apparatus tangle with 1>10.
